visual_thesis: Four contexts with private inputs learn to exchange information through one shared policy and a common task reward.
mechanism_metaphor: One cohesive fourfold paper-relief assembly seen obliquely. Four asymmetric context folds each have a distinct private-input compartment. All four use one common central Shared policy paper core, not four model weights. The four private compartments are visually distinct by geometry, no invented private integers, no alphabetic role names, no duplicate labels. A single message arrow from the first context port (330,260) to the neighboring inbox port (620,330) represents supported information exchange. Other thin paper ties are nondirectional and have no arrowheads. A common score/reward fold sits behind the center; a sorted-output strip below groups the four input shapes in an ordered arrangement, but no fabricated numeric answer. It does not imply a real recorded conversation. Use Private inputs once as a brace across the compartments; render no extra letters or decorative writing. This is a conceptual training example, not evidence of single-agent superiority. Keep the limiting line detached and readable.
